title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issuing the Provisions on the Implementation of Recusal for Court Leading Cadres and Trial and Enforcement Personnel Whose Spouses, Parents, or Children Are Engaged in the Practice of Law
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Issuing the Provisions on the Implementation of Conflict of Interest Avoidance for Leading Officials and Trial and Enforcement Personnel of Courts Whose Spouses, Parents, or Children are Engaged in the Practice of Law

Fa Fa [2020] No. 13

To the High People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; and the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

The Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on the Implementation of Conflict of Interest Avoidance for Leading Officials and Trial and Enforcement Personnel of Courts Whose Spouses, Parents, or Children are Engaged in the Practice of Law are hereby issued to you. They shall come into effect as of May 6, 2020. Please ensure their earnest implementation.

April 17, 2020

Provisions on the Implementation of Conflict of Interest Avoidance for Leading Officials and Trial and Enforcement Personnel of Courts Whose Spouses, Parents, or Children are Engaged in the Practice of Law

In order to maintain judicial fairness and integrity, and to prevent conflicts between the private interests of court leading officials and trial and enforcement personnel and the public interest, these Provisions are formulated in accordance with the Public Servants Law of the People's Republic of China, the Judges Law of the People's Republic of China, and other laws and regulations, taking into account the actual conditions of the people's courts.

Article 1 Where the spouse, parents, children, siblings, spouse's parents, spouse's siblings, children's spouses, or parents of children's spouses of a staff member of a people's court have the status of a lawyer, the staff member shall proactively report to the organizational (personnel) department of the people's court where he or she works.

Article 2 Where the spouse, parents, or children of a leading official or trial and enforcement personnel of a people's court fall under any of the following circumstances, the court leading official or trial and enforcement personnel shall implement conflict of interest avoidance:

(1) They serve as partners or founders of a law firm within the jurisdiction of the people's court where the said leading official or trial and enforcement personnel works; or

(2) They act as litigation representatives or defenders in the capacity of a lawyer within the jurisdiction of the people's court where the said leading official or trial and enforcement personnel works, or provide other paid legal services to litigants in litigation cases.

Article 3 When selecting and appointing cadres, a people's court shall not designate persons who meet the conditions for conflict of interest avoidance as proposed candidates for positions of court leading officials or trial and enforcement personnel.

Article 4 When recruiting or supplementing staff, a people's court shall explain the relevant content of these Provisions to the persons to be recruited or supplemented.

Article 5 A leading official or trial and enforcement personnel of a court who meets the conditions for conflict of interest avoidance shall, within thirty days from the effective date of these Provisions or from the date on which the conditions for conflict of interest avoidance are met, proactively submit an application for conflict of interest avoidance to the court's organizational (personnel) department. The relevant people's court shall, in accordance with relevant provisions, arrange another work position for him or her and determine the position and rank treatment.

Article 6 Where a leading official or trial and enforcement personnel of a court who meets the conditions for conflict of interest avoidance fails to proactively submit an application for conflict of interest avoidance as required, the relevant people's court shall, in accordance with relevant procedures, remove him or her from the leadership position or transfer him or her out of the trial or enforcement post.

Article 7 Where the authority to appoint or remove a leading official or trial and enforcement personnel of a court who should implement conflict of interest avoidance does not lie with the people's court, the relevant people's court shall submit a recommendation to the authority with the power of cadre appointment and removal to handle procedures such as position transfer or removal.

Article 8 Where a leading official or trial and enforcement personnel of a court who meets the conditions for conflict of interest avoidance falls under any of the following circumstances, he or she shall be given criticism and education, admonishment, organizational disposition, or disciplinary action according to the circumstances:

(1) Concealing the fact that his or her spouse, parents, or children are engaged in the practice of law;

(2) Failing to proactively apply for conflict of interest avoidance as required;

(3) Using fraudulent means to circumvent conflict of interest avoidance;

(4) Refusing to comply with organizational adjustments or refusing to handle the handover of official duties; or

(5) Engaging in other acts that violate the provisions on conflict of interest avoidance.

Article 9 Where the spouse, parents, or children of a leading official or trial and enforcement personnel of a court engage in the practice of law within the jurisdiction of the people's court where the said leading official or trial and enforcement personnel works by means such as undisclosed agency, the said court leading official or trial and enforcement personnel shall be ordered to resign from his or her leadership position or be transferred out of the trial or enforcement post. If he or she had knowledge of such conduct, he or she shall be subjected to heavier sanctions in accordance with relevant provisions.

Article 10 Where a court staff member who has been transferred out of a trial or enforcement post due to conflict of interest avoidance has the circumstances giving rise to the conflict of interest avoidance cease to exist, he or she may apply to the court's organizational (personnel) department to be transferred back to a trial or enforcement post.

Article 11 For the purposes of these Provisions, the term "parents" includes biological parents, adoptive parents, and stepparents with a support relationship.
The term "children" includes legitimate children, illegitimate children, adopted children, and stepchildren with a support relationship.
The term "engaged in the practice of law" means serving as a partner or founder of a law firm, or acting as a litigation representative or defender in the capacity of a lawyer, or providing other paid legal services to litigants in litigation cases in the capacity of a lawyer.
The term "leading officials of a court" means members of the leadership group and members of the adjudication committee of a people's court at any level.
The term "trial and enforcement personnel" means members of the leadership group, judges, judge assistants, and enforcement officers in the case-filing, trial, enforcement, trial supervision, and state compensation departments of a people's court at any level.
The term "jurisdiction of the people's court where the person works" includes the jurisdiction of the people's court where the leading official or trial and enforcement personnel works and the jurisdiction of its subordinate people's courts. For staff members of specialized people's courts and other people's courts whose jurisdictional area is inconsistent with the administrative division, the jurisdiction of the people's court where they work shall be determined by the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army and the relevant High People's Court in accordance with relevant provisions or actual circumstances.

Article 12 The interpretation of these Provisions rests with the Supreme People's Court.

Article 13 These Provisions shall come into effect as of May 6, 2020. The Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on the Implementation of Conflict of Interest Avoidance for Leading Officials and Trial and Enforcement Post Judges of Courts Whose Spouses or Children are Engaged in the Practice of Law (for Trial Implementation) (Fa Fa [2011] No. 5) shall be simultaneously abolished.
